arxiv-2307-12179.title: Recognizing Unseen States of Unknown Objects by Leveraging Knowledge Graphs
arxiv-2307-12179.creator: Filippos Gouidis, Konstantinos Papoutsakis, Theodore Patkos, Antonis Argyros, Dimitris Plexousakis
arxiv-2307-12179.description: Abstract We investigate the problem of Object State Classification (OSC) in the context of zero-shot learning. Specifically, we propose the first method for Zero-shot Object-agnostic State Classification (OaSC) that, given an image, infers the state of a single object without relying on the knowledge or the estimation of the object class.

arxiv-2409-04353.title: Whole Heart Perfusion with High-Multiband Simultaneous Multislice Imaging via Linear Phase Modulated Extended Field of View (SMILE)
arxiv-2409-04353.creator: Shen Zhao, Junyu Wang, Xitong Wang, Sizhuo Liu, Quan Chen, Kevin Kai Li, Yoo Jin Lee, Michael Salerno
arxiv-2409-04353.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Shen Zhao, Junyu Wang, Xitong Wang, Sizhuo Liu, Quan Chen, Kevin Kai Li, Yoo Jin Lee, Michael Salerno. 1 Purpose To develop a simultaneous multislice (SMS) first-pass perfusion technique that can achieve whole heart coverage with high multi-band factors, while avoiding the issue of slice leakage.

arxiv-2409-20377.title: Learning thermodynamics and topological order of the 2D XY model with generative real-valued restricted Boltzmann machines
arxiv-2409-20377.creator: Kai Zhang
arxiv-2409-20377.description: Abstract Detecting the topological Kosterlitz–Thouless (KT) transition in the prototypical 2D XY model using unsupervised machine learning methods has long been a challenging problem due to the lack of suitable order parameters. To address this issue, we begin with a conventional real-valued RBM (RBM-xy), which uses exponential conditional probabilities to generate visible units.

arxiv-2501-12852.title: Charging of quantum emitters in hexagonal boron nitride - graphene heterostructures due to electrostatic screening
arxiv-2501-12852.creator: M. K. Prasad, J. P. Goss, J. D. Mar
arxiv-2501-12852.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by M. K. Prasad, J. P. Goss, J. D. Mar. Defect color centers in hexagonal boron nitride (hBN) have gained significant interest as single-photon emitters and spin qubits for applications in a wide range of quantum technologies. As the integration of these solid-state quantum emitters into electronic devices necessitates ctrical ntrol, it is essential to gain a deeper understanding of the mechanisms of charge control for these defect color centers in hBN/graphene heterostructures.

arxiv-2502-18633.title: An NEPv Approach for Feature Selection via Orthogonal OCCA with the ( 2 , 1 ) (2,1) -norm Regularization
arxiv-2502-18633.creator: Li Wang, Lei-Hong Zhang, Ren-Cang Li
arxiv-2502-18633.description: Abstract A novel feature selection model via orthogonal canonical correlation analysis with the ( 2 , 1 ) (2,1) -norm regularization is proposed, and the model is solved by a practical NEPv approach (nonlinear eigenvalue problem with eigenvector dependency), yielding a feature selection method named OCCA-FS.

arxiv-2507-11499.title: Demo: Secure Edge Server for Network Slicing and Resource Allocation in Open RAN
arxiv-2507-11499.creator: Adhwaa Alchaab, Ayman Younis, Dario Pompili ∗ * Department of Electrical and Computer Engineering ∗ * Rutgers University–New Brunswick, NJ, USAE-mails: {adhwaa.alchaab, a.younis, pompili}@rutgers.edu
arxiv-2507-11499.description: Abstract Next-Generation Radio Access Networks (NG-RAN) aim to support diverse vertical applications with strict security, latency, and Service-Level Agreement (SLA) requirements. These demands introduce challenges in securing the infrastructure, allocating resources dynamically, and enabling real-time reconfiguration. This demo presents SnSRIC, a secure and intelligent network slicing framework that mitigates a range of Distributed Denial-of-Service (DDoS) attacks in Open RAN environments.

pmc-10752798.creator: Mengnan Qu, Li Zhou, Xieqiao Yan, Siming Li, Xiaowen Wu, Huayan Xu, Juan Li, Jun Guo, Xu Zhang, Hongzhao Li, Xinan Sheng
pmc-10752798.description: Urothelial carcinoma (UC) represents a common malignancy of the urinary system that can involve the kidneys, ureter, bladder, and urethra. pmc-11344024.title: NLRP3 inflammasome pathway involved in the pathogenesis of metabolic associated fatty liver disease
pmc-11344024.creator: Heba Ahmed Osman, Sawsan M. A. Abuhamdah, Mohammed H. Hassan, Abdelkader Ahmed Hashim, Abdelazeem E. Ahmed, Sameh Salaheldin Elsayed, Samer A. El-Sawy, Mostafa A. Gaber, Marwa Abdelhady
pmc-11344024.description: The prevalence of Metabolic-associated fatty liver disease (MAFLD) has been steadily increasing worldwide, paralleling the global epidemic of obesity and diabetes. It is estimated that approximately one-quarter of the global population is affected by MAFLD. Despite its high prevalence, MAFLD often goes undiagnosed due to the lack of specific symptoms in its early stages.

pmc-11516890.title: Closing the Gap: Implementing Gender-Sensitive Care to Address Healthcare Disparities
pmc-11516890.creator: S Sgraja, J Mollenhauer, U Seeland, M Kloepfer, C Kurscheid, V Amelung
pmc-11516890.description: BackgroundWomen still face a higher mortality rate after a heart attack compared to men, and the reasons remain unknown. The project HeartGap aims to investigate the disparity between evidence-based guidelines and the integration of Gender-Sensitive Care (GSC+) in clinical settings. By exploring healthcare providers’ attitudes and knowledge on GSC+, the project seeks to develop holistic recommendations for its effective implementation.

pmc-11588945.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). DNA aptamers have attracted attention as an alternative modality for biomolecules due to their excellent target binding specificity and thermal stability, and they are also expected to be applied as artificial agonists for receptor proteins. DNA aptamer agonist TD0 targeting the receptor of fibroblast growth factor (FGFR), which plays an important role in the fields of wound healing and regenerative medicine, has been reported to induce cellular responses as well as its native ligands.

pmc-12750361.title: Rational engineering of degradation tail-driven CELMoD–antibody conjugates for precision malignancy therapy
pmc-12750361.creator: Yu Guo, Yi Song, Hanlin Wang, Yang Lu, Jingyu Zhang, Zheyuan Shen, Weijuan Kan, Yuxian Wang, Haiting Duan, Shuangshuang Geng, Bo Wang, Shaoting Li, Bizhi Li, Xi Chen, Shanshan Pei, Luo Fang, Jia Li, Yubo Zhou, Jinxin Che, Xiaowu Dong
pmc-12750361.description: Degrader–antibody conjugates (DACs) represent a promising drug modality for targeting hematological malignancy, but still lack rational design frameworks. Here, we show the strategies of reasonable antibody-degrader compatibility and degradation tail-derived conjugatability through a systematic exploration. Inspired by the success of IKZF1/3 degraders, we sought to explore the potential of cereblon E3 ligase modulators (CELMoDs) in constructing novel conjugates.

pmc-13113617.title: The myth that slow test‐takers are worse students: Implications for time‐limited testing
pmc-13113617.creator: Saul J. Weiner, Yoon Soo Park, Morton Ann Gernsbacher, Kristina H. Petersen
pmc-13113617.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). ProblemTime‐limited testing, a form of assessment in which participants have a fixed amount of time to complete an exam, remains a global standard across the medical education continuum from admissions through licensure and board certification. A wide‐ranging literature, however, documents how speededness, the extent to which a test's time limit alters individual performance, poses a threat to both validity and equity. Specifically, some students require more time than allotted to complete an exam.
